one_line: Voice-assisted public-benefit application with safe agent proposals.
what_it_does: Guides a person through a synthetic benefits application while an agent reads and edits shared form state subject to human confirmation.
leverage_rationale: Structured state-aware tools let an agent inspect remaining sections, navigate, add household/income data, and identify blockers more reliably than DOM driving; human approval remains explicit.
leverage_evidence: Frame sheet shows natural-language request, structured household-member interpretation, update flow, and success state.
About text names state-aware actions and says companion changes require Save change, Need correction, or Cancel.
execution_rationale: The packet coherently demonstrates a central household-add flow from request through confirmation to successful state update, though this is a fictional local demo with no real submission.
execution_evidence: Frames show Emma Carter fields populated and final success confirmation.
About text clearly scopes out real eligibility, enrollment, uploads, and submit.
impact_rationale: Benefits applicants, assisters, and people facing complex healthcare forms have a concrete high-value problem; the demonstrated assistance directly reduces clerical burden while preserving control.
impact_evidence: Pitch and description identify complex public-benefit applications and hours-long workflows.
Human review gate and local-only demo are described.
creativity_rationale: A thoughtful synthesis of voice assistance, shared structured form state, and safety gates for a consequential public-service workflow.
creativity_evidence: Combines optional voice/chat companion with reviewable agent activity and human-only submission.
usability_note: Clear six-section form and confirmation flow; real-world scope is intentionally not implemented.
red_flags: No real eligibility or enrollment integration; evidence is a synthetic local demo.
standouts: Strong human-in-the-loop safety boundary for public benefits.
advance_reason: High-impact, coherent demonstrated workflow with a substantial WebMCP reliability and safety delta.

one_line: Browser extension that infers WebMCP tools from observed site APIs.
what_it_does: Records JSON requests, infers endpoint templates and schemas, and injects replayable native WebMCP tools into sites without developer cooperation.
leverage_rationale: It addresses WebMCP's adoption barrier by turning existing browser traffic into structured agent capabilities; general UI driving cannot comparably provide reusable schemas and page-context replay.
leverage_evidence: Description specifies fetch/XHR observation, endpoint templating, JSON Schema inference, and document.modelContext injection.
Frame shows a job-search site alongside an assistant/task interface, though explicit calls are not visible.
execution_rationale: The concept and extension architecture are coherent, but frame evidence mainly shows a repeated browsing/task state rather than the extension's inferred tools executing end-to-end.
execution_evidence: About text gives a detailed MV3 architecture and site pooling behavior.
Contact sheet shows browsing workflow but no clear completed search or explicit tool trace.
impact_rationale: If reliable, it could make agent interfaces available across the existing web, benefiting users and developers who cannot retrofit every site.
impact_evidence: Description targets nearly all sites already making API calls and removes per-endpoint wiring.
Architecture includes filtering trackers and preserving cookies/auth context.
creativity_rationale: Highly original solution to the chicken-and-egg WebMCP adoption problem, with ambitious automatic schema inference and runtime injection.
creativity_evidence: Core idea is automatic conversion of observed APIs into native tools without site cooperation.
usability_note: Promised no-config workflow is compelling; observed packet does not establish reliability across diverse sites.
red_flags: Security and correctness risks of replaying captured auth headers and third-party APIs are not resolved by the packet.
standouts: Directly tackles WebMCP distribution and adoption rather than building one more app.
advance_reason: Exceptional WebMCP ambition and novelty; execution evidence is thinner than the claim.

one_line: Local-first recovery workspace that turns post-disaster chaos into reviewed plans.
what_it_does: Structures incident facts, evidence, deadlines, recovery tasks, and communication drafts through a human-gated agent workflow.
leverage_rationale: Shared validated command state, structured receipts, and review gates make agent assistance substantially safer and more repeatable than UI scraping in a sensitive workflow.
leverage_evidence: Description says UI and WebMCP route through the same validated command pipeline.
Features include pending_review plans, audit events, and grounded dates.
execution_rationale: Strongly specified and apparently coherent, but the packet's frame sheet shows primarily an onboarding choice screen and does not demonstrate the recovery workflow end-to-end.
execution_evidence: About text details intake, evidence ledger, staged plans, drafts, and persistence.
Frame sheet visibly shows Choose how to begin but no completed recovery plan.
impact_rationale: Disaster survivors face an acute, specific administrative burden; turning chaotic facts into prioritized, sourced actions is credible high-value help.
impact_evidence: Description targets displaced households and cognitive overload.
Plans cite Ready.gov, FEMA, and Red Cross guidance.
creativity_rationale: Memorable combination of local-first privacy, evidence ledger, bounded drafting, and strict approval in disaster recovery.
creativity_evidence: Explicitly separates unconfirmed facts, agent proposals, and human approvals.
usability_note: Calm WCAG-oriented design is claimed; observed evidence is limited to onboarding.
red_flags: Core recovery flow is not visibly demonstrated in the supplied frame evidence.
standouts: Safety and provenance model fits a high-stakes recovery context.
advance_reason: Very strong audience/problem fit and thoughtful agent-state design despite thin end-to-end visual evidence.

one_line: Editable beat studio where agents arrange individual sounds with humans.
what_it_does: Builds instrumentals by placing notes and drum samples on a timeline, allowing agent-directed edits rather than black-box audio generation.
leverage_rationale: Structured musical primitives and timeline state make agent composition precise and editable; general UI driving would be markedly more cumbersome, though the same outcome is possible.
leverage_evidence: Description distinguishes individual sound-unit arrangement from rigid generated audio.
Frame sheet shows blank sequencer progressing to a structured multitrack pattern.
execution_rationale: Frames show a coherent editor workflow from empty timeline to populated repeating arrangement with transport controls.
execution_evidence: Contact sheet visibly shows colored events added across grid rows and a stable arrangement.
About text describes editable timeline composition.
impact_rationale: Beginners, indie artists, hobbyists, and content creators have a clear desire for fast editable instrumental creation; the product addresses control and iteration.
impact_evidence: Description names target users and contrasts with rigid black-box generation.
Visible sequencer demonstrates an editable arrangement.
creativity_rationale: Fresh interaction model treats the agent as a musical arranging partner operating on atomic sounds, not a generator of opaque finished audio.
creativity_evidence: Core distinction is agent composition of individual notes/drums with human iteration.
usability_note: Timeline, track controls, and transport are visibly coherent; exact agent affordances are not shown.
red_flags: No explicit tool-call trace visible in frame sheet.
standouts: Atomic editable collaboration is a meaningful alternative to black-box music generation.
advance_reason: Strong visible editor execution and creative premise with meaningful WebMCP-enabled precision.

one_line: Stellar marketplace that dynamically turns settled paid APIs into WebMCP tools.
what_it_does: Catalogs payable endpoints by real settlement and trust history, then registers marketplace entries as callable tools for agents.
leverage_rationale: Dynamic tool creation from real payment-backed marketplace state links agent capability, trust, and payment in a way ordinary UI automation cannot reproduce comparably.
leverage_evidence: Description says tools are dynamically registered from live Bazaar results and real on-chain USDC settlements.
Frame shows agent-tool/developer documentation and live-server tooling context.
execution_rationale: The architecture is ambitious and the packet describes live infrastructure, but demo_alive is unknown and frames do not clearly show a completed paid call.
execution_evidence: About text describes facilitator, Bazaar, trust filtering, and dynamic registration.
FACTS marks demo_alive unknown.
impact_rationale: A trusted payment rail and marketplace could unlock useful agent commerce for API sellers and buyers, though value depends on live ecosystem reliability.
impact_evidence: Description identifies real sellers, endpoints, settlements, and USDC movement.
Developer docs claim endpoint gating in under a minute.
creativity_rationale: Novel fusion of on-chain payment history, trust-ranked API discovery, and dynamic WebMCP capability registration.
creativity_evidence: Marketplace itself writes tools based on settlement data rather than static developer declarations.
usability_note: Conceptual flow is clear, but unknown live demo status and payment complexity reduce confidence.
red_flags: Submission explicitly describes infrastructure built for months; demo liveness is unknown.
No visible completed payment/tool execution in reviewed frame evidence.
standouts: Strongest marketplace-level WebMCP concept in the packet.
advance_reason: Exceptional leverage and creativity merit advancement, subject to eligibility and live-demo verification.

one_line: Local-first piano roll for safe, reversible human-agent composition.
what_it_does: Lets an agent inspect live musical state and make deterministic harmony, bass, arrangement, and transform edits with explanations and undo.
leverage_rationale: Live shared state, deterministic musical operations, verification, and reversible edits create a materially better agent collaboration than generic UI control.
leverage_evidence: Description lists read/analyze/edit/verify tools over live project state.
Every persistent AI edit has a plain-language explanation and Undo.
execution_rationale: The written scope is coherent, but no video frame sheet was submitted and only one packaging screenshot is available, so end-to-end execution is capped.
execution_evidence: About text provides detailed editor and tool behavior.
FACTS state no video and only one gallery image; no frame evidence to verify core workflow.
impact_rationale: Beginners and intermediate musicians can benefit from understandable theory-aware assistance while retaining creative control.
impact_evidence: Description identifies intimidation and opaque generation as the user problem.
Features support auditionable alternatives and MIDI export.
creativity_rationale: The reversible, explainable musical co-editing model is a fresh and ambitious interaction design.
creativity_evidence: Deterministic harmony plus agent edits and one-click undo are distinctive.
usability_note: Claims strong controls and accessibility across pointer/MIDI input, but visual evidence is absent.
red_flags: No submitted video frame sheets; core product cannot be visually checked.
standouts: Explainable and undoable agent edits preserve the musician's creative loop.
advance_reason: Strong concept and WebMCP fit, but thin execution evidence warrants verification in the next stage.

one_line: Two independent agents negotiate and redline a shared lease renewal.
what_it_does: Tenant and landlord agents use six page tools to propose, counter, concede, accept, and finalize terms against shared Firestore state.
leverage_rationale: The product's core interaction—independent agents coordinating only through shared page tools—is impractical to replicate comparably with a general UI-driving agent; shared live state is the mechanism.
leverage_evidence: Description explicitly says agents never talk directly and both read/write the same Firestore document via page tools.
Frames show negotiation activity, structured lease terms, shared surface, and redline-style progression.
execution_rationale: Frames visibly progress from landing page to lease case to negotiation workspace with activity and structured terms; the author also documents catching and correcting a false shell-based test.
execution_evidence: Contact sheet shows lease renewal case and live negotiation dashboard.
Description names six tools and redline diffs; acknowledges prior invalid test and tool-only correction.
impact_rationale: Lease renewal negotiation is a concrete costly pain point for tenants and landlords; shared redlines and bounded goals offer credible value.
impact_evidence: Pitch and description target lease back-and-forth and show a concrete Unit 48 scenario.
Negotiation history is logged as amendment-like diffs.
creativity_rationale: Memorable multi-agent negotiation mediated through browser-native tools and a shared deal surface, pursued with strong interaction specificity.
creativity_evidence: Independent tenant/landlord agents, concession actions, and redline history form an original interaction model.
usability_note: Shared terms and activity log make the negotiation legible; consequential lease use would still need safeguards.
red_flags: Initial demo test bypassed WebMCP via exposed Firebase key; author says this was discovered and corrected, but security deserves Stage 2 checks.
standouts: Direct, unusually strong demonstration of WebMCP as a coordination substrate.
advance_reason: Top-tier leverage with visible product progression, honest testing caveat, and a highly memorable concept.

one_line: Source-grounded contract decision room with human approval gates.
what_it_does: Analyzes local documents, surfaces clause findings with exact evidence, and lets agents propose while humans resolve risks and prepare unsigned packets.
leverage_rationale: Narrow structured tools over shared source-grounded state preserve proposal/approval boundaries and produce receipts; generic UI automation is less reliable in this high-stakes workflow.
leverage_evidence: Description lists six tools with closed schemas, effects, structured receipts, and explicit sent:false/signed:false states.
Frames show Northstar review metrics, exclusivity finding, and transition to exact-source bounded analysis.
execution_rationale: The packet shows a coherent contract review progression and detailed safeguards, but no gallery images and no explicit tool-call trace limit observed execution certainty.
execution_evidence: Contact sheet shows Know before you sign and Exact source, bounded analysis states.
About text specifies local OCR, findings, audit events, and approval flow.
impact_rationale: Contract teams have a real need to identify risk without confusing AI prose with approval; source-linked findings and human decisions directly address it.
impact_evidence: Description targets risk, authority, and action confusion in agreements.
Synthetic Northstar case demonstrates auto-renewal, exclusivity, payment, cure, and liability findings.
creativity_rationale: A strong, safety-conscious decision-room model that treats provenance and authority as first-class interaction design.
creativity_evidence: Exact governing clause beside each finding and unsigned receipt boundary are distinctive.
usability_note: Progressive review UI and source excerpts appear legible; no gallery images were submitted.
red_flags: No gallery images; tool execution is inferred from packaging/text rather than an explicit visible call log.
standouts: Excellent separation of agent proposal from human approval and signing.
advance_reason: Credible high-stakes use case with strong provenance and safety architecture; verify tool-only execution.

one_line: Runtime that learns, caches, validates, and repairs browser workflows.
what_it_does: Routes tasks native-WebMCP-first, then reuses versioned semantic browser skills and repairs failed steps after UI changes.
leverage_rationale: Persistent validated skills and targeted repair address repeatability and resilience beyond one-off UI automation; WebMCP is the first-class routing layer.
leverage_evidence: Description specifies Native WebMCP → Cached Web Skill → DOM fallback priority ladder.
Frame sheet shows runtime/taskboard onboarding but does not clearly expose tool calls; written claim includes 11-action Learn–Reuse–Repair flow.
execution_rationale: The architecture and claimed taskboard flow are coherent, but visual contact sheets primarily show a choose-how-to-begin screen rather than the full learn/reuse/repair completion.
execution_evidence: About text details IndexedDB versioning, validation, fingerprints, and targeted repair.
Frame sheet visibly shows an onboarding state, not end-to-end repair.
impact_rationale: Agents and teams repeatedly performing browser workflows have a real reliability and token-cost problem that cached, repairable skills directly target.
impact_evidence: Description identifies rediscovery, brittleness, and UI-change failures.
Features include inspectable logs, timings, validation, and immutable versions.
creativity_rationale: Ambitious and original synthesis of WebMCP routing, learned semantic workflows, dependency fingerprints, and surgical repair.
creativity_evidence: The explicit fallback ladder and dependency-only repair model are memorable innovations.
usability_note: Inspector and validation afford trust, but full flow was not visibly demonstrated.
red_flags: No gallery images; visual evidence is repetitive onboarding rather than the claimed 11-action flow.
standouts: Treats browser skills as durable, versioned assets instead of disposable traces.
advance_reason: Very strong agent-infrastructure concept and leverage; Stage 2 should verify actual repair behavior.

one_line: Agent-native pantry planner that prioritizes expiry and derives shopping lists.
what_it_does: Maintains pantry and meal state, plans expiry-first dinners, consolidates shopping needs, and keeps final judgment with the human.
leverage_rationale: A typed stateful contract compresses repeated pantry reads, planning, and list derivation into structured calls, but a capable general agent could achieve much of this with UI friction.
leverage_evidence: Description specifies eight document.modelContext tools with JSON Schema and structured JSON results.
Agent workflow spans pantry read, seven-day plan, shopping derivation, and repeated updates.
execution_rationale: The written scope is coherent, but no video frame sheet was submitted and the packet includes no visual proof of the planning result.
execution_evidence: About text explains human and agent responsibilities and tool table.
FACTS show no video frame sheets were submitted.
impact_rationale: Households have a real recurring food-waste and meal-planning burden; expiry-aware plans and consolidated lists offer credible practical value.
impact_evidence: Description identifies expiry triage, weekly planning, and food waste.
Human swaps and store checkoffs preserve realistic user judgment.
creativity_rationale: A useful agent-native application of stateful planning to kitchens, with a clear division of labor, though the category is familiar.
creativity_evidence: Expiry-first planning plus aisle-consolidated list as one structured workflow.
usability_note: The described human/agent split is understandable; product usability cannot be visually checked.
red_flags: No submitted video frames or visible outcome evidence.
standouts: Clear everyday stateful-planning use case for WebMCP.
advance_reason: Good concept and audience fit, but execution evidence is too thin relative to the packet's claims.
